newsitem.title: USA: U.S. officials head to Asia on financial services.
newsitem.headline: U.S. officials head to Asia on financial services.

text.p: Deputy U.S. Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang and Assistant Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner head to Asia next week to discuss financial services deregulation, the U.S. Trade Representative's office said Thursday.

The two U.S. officials will be in Tokyo on Monday to discuss the status of World Trade Organization talks to open up financial services markets. Lang will also meet Japanese automobile and other industry executives to discuss deregulation issues, the USTR said.
Lang plans to go to Seoul and Manila on Tuesday and Thursday. He will hold talks on financial services in Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and India.

The United States is looking for some improved offers from Asian countries to open up their financial services sectors. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said this week that the United States was ready to be flexible but would not sign a deal that did not meet U.S. interests.

The financial crisis in Thailand has heightened concerns in some Asian countries about efforts to ease trade rules in financial services. Critics argue that foreign access to their markets could hurt domestic banks and that fickle speculative capital could threaten security.
